2609.10434.title: Do speech foundation models really learn words?
2609.10434.paper_summary: Self-supervised speech foundation models are now used in a wide array of downstream applications, including traditional speech recognition and as the basis for tokens in speech-aware language models. Attempts to understand their usefulness have largely focused on probing their representations' ability to discriminate phonemes and words. However, discriminative ability for words need not imply specialized representation of words per se. Good discrimination of words may be explained by good encoding of word form (phonemes) rather than form-independent word representations encoding identity or syntactic/semantic properties. By partialling out phoneme information using residualization, we show that, in later layers, HuBERT and wav2vec 2.0 do in general learn representations which encode words with reasonable fidelity independently of local phonetic content. We show that this simple approach to disentanglement can enhance higher-order linguistic information in word discovery tasks.
2609.10434.paper_summary_zh: 自我監督的語音基礎模型現在被廣泛應用於各種下游應用，包括傳統的語音識別和作為語音感知語言模型中標記的基礎。對於理解它們的有用性，嘗試主要集中在探測它們的表示能力，以區分音素和單詞。然而，對於單詞的區分能力並不一定意味著對單詞本身的專門表示。對單詞的良好區分可以通過對單詞形式（音素）的良好編碼來解釋，而不是通過形式獨立的單詞表示來編碼身份或句法/語義屬性。通過使用殘差化來部分去除音素信息，我們顯示，在後面的層中，HuBERT 和 wav2vec 2.0 確實學習到的表示能夠以合理的保真度獨立於局部語音內容來編碼單詞。我們顯示，這種簡單的解耦方法可以在單詞發現任務中增強高階語言信息。
2609.10434.author: Robin Huo et.al.
